title: Responder Evidence & Escalation Curriculum: Playbook for Oncall Operators
author: Maya Patel
content:
SUMMARY
This document is a combined operational playbook and training curriculum for oncall responders focused on evidence collection, rapid escalation, and consistent customer communications. It establishes:
- a single evidence collection lifecycle for all severity classes;
- role-based responsibilities during triage and escalation;
- a runbook template optimized for fast capture of forensic artifacts;
- standardized status-page and customer message templates;
- a curriculum and scoreboard for game day exercises intended to certify responders.

SCOPE AND AUDIENCE
- Scope: All incidents that touch Redwood inference serving (hosted, dedicated, private). Applies to SREs, oncall engineers, support L2, and incident commanders.
- Audience: oncall responders, incident commanders, SOC/Customer Success for customer notices, and managers reviewing postmortems.

GOALS AND PRINCIPLES
1) Collect minimal but sufficient evidence in first 15 minutes to enable root-cause follow-ups.
2) Keep customer communications factual and consistent; one canonical status message per cadence.
3) Escalate based on impact metrics (see Severity Matrix).
4) Continuous training: every responder must pass the Evidence Collection practical twice yearly.

SEVERITY MATRIX (DECISION RULES)
1. Sev 1 (Critical): Complete service outage or >40% error rate across customer-facing RPCs for >5 minutes or major data loss.
2. Sev 2 (High): Significant customer impact (single region degraded, >5% user impact, or severe latency degradation).
3. Sev 3 (Medium): Partial feature regression, isolated customer issues.
4. Sev 4 (Low): Cosmetic problems, developer/non-urgent requests.

Escalation trigger examples: 
- Auto-alert: sustained error-rate >20% for 2 minutes (trigger to oncall primary).
- Manual: Customer escalates via CSM > immediate engage L2 + oncall.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES (QUICK REFERENCE)
- Primary Responder (P): Acknowledge alert, collect evidence checklist v1.0, maintain live notes.
- Secondary (S): Validate forking issues, run containment actions, prepare rollback if required.
- Incident Commander (IC): Orchestrate comms, escalate to oncall lead, declare bridge if Sev >=2.
- Forensics Owner: Post-incident artifact curation and handoff to RCA team.
- Customer Comms Lead: Drafts status updates and liaises with CSM.

EVIDENCE COLLECTION LIFECYCLE (FIRST 60 MINUTES)
1) Acknowledge & Timestamp: record incident start time and acknowledge in PagerDuty/Slack.
2) Capture service-level snapshot (within 5 minutes):
   - Running deployments and commit IDs (kubectl get deploys / git tags)
   - Active model versions and model-serving configs (model catalog link + model_id)
   - Node/gpu health and utilization: nvidia-smi snapshots, top output
3) Pump logs to a short-term bucket for analysis (CLI snippet below).
4) Retrieve sample failed request payloads (scrub PII).
5) KV cache and prefix entries snapshot (if applicable) — note sequence numbers.
6) Telemetry snapshot: recent p95/p99 latency, token-per-second throughput.
7) Save a short trace/span export covering representative traces (10–30s).
8) Onboard Forensics Owner for longer retention beyond auto-rotations.

Required artifacts checklist (first-pass):
- Incident timeline (text notes)
- Error-rate graph (png)
- Top 5 stack traces (file)
- Sample request/response (scrubbed)
- Deployment manifest + commit hash
- GPU/host health dumps (nvidia-smi, dmesg if kernel signals)
- Span/trace export (zip)
- Relevant config snapshots (quantization profiles, batching config)

RUNBOOK TEMPLATE (USE THIS AS THE DEFAULT)
1) Title: [service] - short description
2) Symptom summary: one-line
3) First-responder checklist (5 bullets)
4) Quick containment actions (ordered)
5) Evidence artifacts to gather (list with filenames)
6) Escalation matrix (names + contact)
7) Recovery steps (ordered, reversible if possible)
8) Post-incident tasks and handoff

Example runbook snippet for latency spike:
- Title: inference-gateway - sudden p99 increase after deploy
- Symptom: p99 latency increased from 110ms -> 950ms at 10:12 UTC
- First-responder checklist: 1) Confirm p99 from console, 2) Capture traces, 3) Snapshot model version in use, 4) If rollout active: pause canary.
- Quick containment: revert rollout OR route to next-lower-cost model variant (fallback).

CLI SNIPPETS & COMMANDS (EXAMPLE)
- Capture deployment and commit: kubectl get deploy -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, image: .spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}' > /tmp/deploys.json
- Export traces: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "${OBS_API}/v1/traces?since=15m" -o /tmp/traces.zip
- Scrub and store logs: scripts/collect_logs.sh --service inference-gateway --since 15m --bucket temp-incident-logs

STATUS PAGE & CUSTOMER COMMUNICATIONS
Principles: single source of truth (status.redwood.example), short and factual, one message per cadence (initial/updates/resolved), avoid speculation.

Status message templates (replace placeholders):
- Initial (Sev 1):
  Title: "Partial outage: Inference API errors for some customers"
  Body: "We are investigating elevated 5xx errors affecting request traffic to the Inference API. Impact: some customers may experience failed requests and degraded latency. We have engaged our oncall team and are collecting diagnostics. Next update: in 15 minutes."

- Update (containment in progress):
  Title: "Update: Containment actions underway"
  Body: "We have identified a likely regression in model-serving batching and have paused the canary rollout. Fallback routing is enabled for high-priority traffic. We continue to collect traces and will provide further updates every 30 minutes."

- Resolved:
  Title: "Resolved: Inference API incident"
  Body: "The issue has been mitigated. Root cause analysis is in progress; we will publish a post-incident summary within 72 hours. Customers who experienced errors may see transient retry behavior."

Customer-private template for impacted customers (use only with CS review):
  Subject: "Redwood Inference — Incident affecting request success for [customer-name]"
  Body: "We experienced transient errors between [start] and [end] UTC that affected some requests. We have taken [actions]. We are performing a root cause analysis and will share findings and any relevant mitigations within 72 hours. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this email or contact your CSM."

COMMUNICATION CADENCE
- Sev 1: initial within 5–10 minutes, then every 15–30 minutes until containment, then hourly during RCA; resolved + 72h RCA.
- Sev 2: initial within 20 minutes, then 30–60 minute cadence.
- Sev 3/4: oncall summary and postmortem if customer-facing.

ESCALATION RULES (CONCRETE)
- If evidence collection fails (missing artifacts) within 15 minutes, escalate to Secondary and IC.
- If impact crosses 3+ customers with SLO breaches, escalate to Platform Lead and CS Director.
- If incident enters hotfix/rollback, open a separate change ticket and notify Change Control.

GAME DAY CURRICULUM (EXERCISE DESIGN)
Purpose: validate people/process/tools under pressure. Exercises are graded for both operational correctness and evidence completeness.
Frequency: quarterly for oncall teams; new hires join bi-monthly.
Exercise types:
- Simulated KV-cache poison (severity: 2): focus on quick detection and rollback.
- Token storm (rate-limited throttle) (severity: 2/3): validate autoscaling and fallback routing.
- Silent degradation (quality regression) (severity: 3): tests triage of quality alerts and canary inspection.

Scoring rubric (per exercise):
- Acknowledge time: 0–10 points (faster is better).
- Evidence checklist completeness: 0–40 points (each artifact weighted).
- Correct escalation & comms pacing: 0–30 points.
- Post-exercise RCA + action items: 0–20 points.
Passing score: 75/100. Teams that fail must remediate gaps within 30 days and re-certify.

TRAINING MILESTONES (RESPONDER PATH)
- Level 1 (Observer): completes 1 tabletop, reads runbook templates, passes multiple-choice quiz.
- Level 2 (Responder): completes two supervised game days, demonstrates evidence capture.
- Level 3 (Incident Commander): leads two exercises, drafts postmortem and customer comms.
Certification validity: 12 months.

POST-INCIDENT: HANDOFF AND RCA
1) Forensics Owner packages artifacts in centralized incident bucket, tags severity and retention (30/90/365 days per policy).
2) IC authors postmortem using the canonical template within 72 hours (summary, timeline, impact, root cause, mitigations, owners, verification plan).
3) Actions are tracked in a dedicated JIRA board with required auto-reminders for owners.
4) Postmortem review: run monthly table reviews with SRE, Platform, and CS for customer-impacting incidents.

OBSERVABILITY & AUTOMATION CHECKPOINTS
- Ensure runbook execution is reproducible via CLI / scripts (no manual-only steps).
- Automate evidence collection where possible: trace-dump, logs snapshot, and config export scripts must be in /automation/incident/
- Auto-attach evidence to incident ticket via webhook (PagerDuty -> JIRA integration).

MEASURABLES AND KPIS
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA): target < 2 minutes for alerts routed to oncall.
- Mean time to evidence capture (MTTEC): target < 15 minutes for first-pass checklist.
- Evidence completeness rate: goal > 95% across Sev1/2 incidents.
- Game day pass rate: target team-level 90% per quarter.

APPENDIX: QUICK CHECKLIST (PRINTABLE)
1) Acknowledge alert & note timestamp.
2) Grab deployment manifest + commit hash.
3) Export 15m traces and top 20 logs.
4) Capture GPU/host health snapshot.
5) Collect sample failed requests and scrub.
6) Post update to status page (if Sev >=2) and set next update cadence.
7) Escalate to IC when containment is not visible in 15 minutes.

OWNERSHIP & CONTACTS (EXAMPLE TABLE - TEXT)
- Oncall Primary: @oncall-primary (pagerduty)
- Oncall Secondary: @oncall-secondary
- Incident Commander: eng-sre-ic@redwood.example
- Customer Comms Lead: cs-comm@redwood.example
- Forensics Owner: forensics@redwood.example

RELATED TOOLS & ARTIFACT LOCATIONS
- Incident notes: /confluence/incidents/{incident-id}
- Evidence storage: gs://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}
- Automation scripts: git@github.com:redwood/ops-automation.git/tree/main/incident

CHANGELOG
- 2025-10-08: initial draft and curriculum design (Maya Patel)
- 2026-02-14: updated severity triggers, added game day rubric and CLI snippets (Maya Patel)

If you are reading this as a responder preparing for your rotation: bookmark the "Quick checklist" section and ensure your PagerDuty and Slack memberships are current. If you have suggestions for the curriculum or automation, file a PR against the automation repo and tag the oncall team.
